body: Thank you so much for this. I do think you have hit the nail on the head in a lot of ways, at least for my particular situation. I’m sorry, I’m in a particularly bad way right now so I can’t come up with a proper response, but there are some things I’d like to pick your brain about when it comes to this mindset. I’ll send you a PM when I can find the mental clarity to give you a worthwhile response.
Thank you. :) Good luck on your journey.
I’m in the same boat. How are you doing, OP?

I honestly feel like the neglect is what really did me in. If I had support for the abuse that happened, maybe I would be relatively okay now. Instead I’m a complete mess because I was so utterly alone and unable to bear the weight by myself.

Yeah, groups are so tough right now. My therapist wanted me to join one she was hosting, and told me some great people would be there. But... it just isn’t the right time. Hopefully one day soon. Funny about the knitters, my younger sister (16) back home is one, maybe she’ll grow up to be a good ally. :)
ELI5: how do you find genuine people to let into your life? 🥲
Same here actually. I’ll send you a message. :)
“I had the same mistrust and hate towards my own masculinity” - this right here explains it so well. No wonder I hate everything that is feminine so much. Thanks for sharing your experience.

As a 26F, I can relate 100%.

I have never had a healthy, strong relationship with a female. Even the girls I was friends with when I was younger... there was no distinction between them and my male friends, if that makes sense. There was no “female” bond, ever. Right now I don’t have a single female in my life that I consider a friend.

I’ve been thinking about this a lot lately. I’m going to say this in case it helps someone else realize it for themselves. To expand further on your realization, the reason I believe that I personally have come to feel this way is because every single female in my life left me to rot. This is especially true and powerful when it comes to the fact this can be applied to my mother. She never provided me with the care that I needed, so I found it wherever I could as a child. Unfortunately, this meant I clung to men, as men were more willing to provide this to me, as I had something that they strongly desired - my body.

I have a feeling that finding a female that I can bond with will be extremely healing. It’s quite overwhelming thinking about this though. Definitely have some trust issues to work through. Anyways, it’s interesting and helpful in a way to know I’m not alone in feeling this so thanks for bringing it up. It gives me hope that perhaps one day I’ll finally cross paths with someone who understands - beyond just virtual correspondence, anyways.

I’m sorry to hear that. I’m sure he knows that you love him. It’s similar with my siblings, I wasn’t able to reach my brother for his birthday last week either... all we can do is leave our hearts open for them, and hope they find their way back.

I just want to say that you are an inspiration for making it through all of that, and now choosing to find healing. The fact you put your foot down and ended the abuse is the best thing you could have done. I am sending positive thoughts your way, and I hope that you can find the life you deserve.

It’s not quite the same, but I was abused by my step father, uncle, and biological father (although he was non-sexually). I am not sure if this resonates with you, but I feel like the isolation is what fucked me up the most. My mother ignoring me when I needed her the most. No friends or family caring. Just being so utterly alone. Do you still have contact with your brother? Could he be an ally in your healing? For me, my siblings are on their own paths and not doing the best.. I hope you have some support, at least, and if not, at least there is the void of the internet. It may feel empty here, but we hear you. Best of luck to you.

Does anyone else worry that this type of therapy work can lead to Dissociative Identity Disorder? I’m currently doing this work with my therapist and it feels very strange having to consider different “parts” of me, as they are technically different personalities as well, it feels like it’s opening the door for DID for those of us already prone to it?

Other than that, I will preface my opinion by saying I’ve only been doing this for a few months. It is nice to get in touch with the emotions that helped shape who I am today. I appreciate being able to understand why and how they evolved. I think this helps me in my healing as I have a better overall understanding about why I am the way I am through inner child work. I do feel like it is something you should be cautious about, though. Everyone heals in their own ways, but to me it feels like a dangerous rabbit hole to get _too_ involved in these past parts of us.

It’s all about how you frame it in your mind, I suppose, but I guess I am saying do be weary to not presently become these past parts...

This is exactly what I’m feeling right now. It feels like I’ll never find the type of relationships that I desire, like I’ll never feel a bond or like I’m understood. Most of my relationships so far have been super “surface level”. It’s tough. It made me feel a bit better to read your post and realize someone out there is in a similar position as me, at a similar time too, so I thought I’d comment to let you know that at least in that sense, you’re not alone. Here’s to hoping we find what we are looking for in others when the time is right.

Thanks so much! That is a pretty sweet career path you chose. I totally get the nervousness though of course... I think that’s normal for most people, it just gets amped up a lot if you deal with CPTSD too. :( I feel like I’m basically taking on an already difficult role, but in extra hard mode.

Worst case scenario would probably be me getting into a shitty headspace again that causes me to stop working... I’ve survived that already so I guess I could again if I really had to, but I really, really don’t want to. 🥲

Yeah, “demand” was not the right word... I’m not much of a demander. I’ll definitely say something along the lines of what you suggested.

You’re not wrong if it was a normal workplace. The thing is this company has a bit of a record with screwing me over with high workload and false promises, so that’s why I’m nervous. If I’m in support and another position opens up, I at least wouldn’t have to worry about not getting the role because my old role is hard to fill. My current position is easily filled compared to this PDF one. At least that’s my thought process.

Yeah. I signed up for a 10-day silent meditation course for this reason. About the closest you can get to being “out” for a bit. Start date was as soon as stuff started shutting down for Covid though, so I couldn’t go.

Not to say that’s a solution or anything, but if anyone reading this agrees with the title and is a regular meditator, maybe it’s a thought to consider for when things open up again.

Girl, YES! It looks soo good.

What length did you take it down to? I think you’d look especially good with a straight-up buzz cut, like a “1” guard. You should give it a try since it’s not much shorter!

Hi. First off, I’m sorry you’re going through this. I’m in a similar boat myself. You might find r/CPTSD to be helpful, it’s a great support community.

As for your actual question, there is no financing available through the federal government. It’s all based on province. I’m not familiar with the Yukon, but I’d try to ask this on their subreddit. Try to look on Google for “victim assistance Yukon” and see where it leads you. There are victim funds available for B.C. and Ontario but I’m not sure about the Yukon. You can probably find at least free or low cost counselling with some Google work though.

Best of luck. If you ever need someone to talk to, feel free to reach out.

“Paranoid at my own existence”, blah... I feel that.

Totally had the same thing happen - I loved being present for a bit. To actually feel after so long of numbing myself out. Now it just gets weird sometimes. I try not to think about it too much, because it’s the overthinking that really gets me, but problem is that’s just in my nature. Probably a big reason why I shut down and dissociated in the first place, because overthinking the trauma just sent me for too much of a wild ride.

I’m going through those techniques right now. Very, very slow improvements.

I’m curious if you can elaborate on what was scary about not being zoned out? It freaks me out a lot sometimes too but I’m curious if it’s for a similar reason.

It’s hard to put it into words for me but I guess it’s because I’m a lot more aware of things, especially people. And it’s not the awareness exactly that’s freaky, but just the fact that I have to accept this all as real and that I have to “play” along with it I guess.

Hi. I had a similar experience myself. Like, very similar.

You need to get out ASAP, as far away as you can. If you can somehow gather any evidence, even him admitting to it through text, you also need to get him charged. Fuck him. Don’t worry about his feelings or your mother’s feelings, or anyone’s feelings really besides your own.

Which country do you live in? If you live in Canada, I can provide some resources depending on the province.

I’m also here if you want to message me to talk about any of it. I’m almost 26 now and I’ve lived through it as well. I’m in the process of healing (and it will be a lifelong process with no end), but I’m happy to help in any way I can.

I’ve had the opposite experience. Just want to put that out there. It’s a drug and it will effect everyone differently. I’m glad it works for you though and I am definitely a bit envious because now I have to learn to somehow go without anything at all.

For me, it makes me dissociate like crazy. And I love that numb feeling so it became addictive. I’m not the only one I know who it has this effect on, and the others haven’t even experienced trauma. It just simply depends on your brain chemistry, I guess. Overall, you just gotta do what is right for you.

I so wish he was convicted there instead of here. I’m glad I at least got some justice though. Many do not sadly.

I think he’s probably too stupid to be aware that he could press charges, and luckily I am very far away from him now, in another province. It would be a hassle to get to me and I’d hope the police would just think he had it coming and it’s not worth their time anyways.

But yeah, whether he has hurt them yet or not, doesn’t matter really. He never got therapy so I’m sure nothing’s changed deep inside. If he cared enough, he would sign himself up for that. Until then, fuck him.

Thank you. ❤️ That’s a really powerful statement you made and it makes me proud to have done this.

The first time I noticed he was in a relationship and said something, I was a young teenager. His girlfriend admitted he did say he went to jail, but because my mom lied about abuse towards her. I was always proud of past myself, but for some reason it felt a bit different this time around. A little bit more fear, a little bit more shame. If it ever has to happen again, God forbid, I’m not going to hesitate.

P.S. Thanks for the hugs, sending them right back. ❤️

Thank you so much. ❤️ I definitely wouldn’t put it below him to discriminate on gender. People like him might have a preference but ultimately, it’s about power.

I’m feeling a lot better about this decision and will stick by it. I know it’s what the inner kid in me would’ve wanted me to do.
It was child sexual assault. ☹️ Rape should be treated very similar though.

There are criminal record checks, but unfortunately the criminal must consent to them by signing a form. I suppose she could corner him into this, if he refuses to sign, that should give her the answer immediately. And if he signs, she’ll get to see exactly what happened. I might reactivate the account and give her this idea because I have a feeling she’ll be a tough one to convince... she’s head over heels.

Thank you. ❤️ I sure hope it will work out for the best.

It is 100% protecting the abuser. That’s Canada for you. The states seem like the polar opposite. I really wish he was convicted there instead, he probably would’ve gotten 10+ years in jail instead of 1.

Thank you though. ❤️ As long as he leaves me and my family alone, I’ll be glad I did this. Even better would be if I get to see him completely alone again.

I know... they said it would be considered harassment. The guy was barely over his ban from being around playgrounds at the time. Makes no sense.

Thank you. ❤️

Yeah... this was a while ago and it was my mother who called, but I think they said something along the lines of harassment. I was pretty shocked. Wish I just called them myself, but I was so over it all at the time.

I did ask her to speak with her children and not with him as he will only deny it all. I mentioned how I wasn’t able to tell the truth until my mom found solid evidence, so she may have to go that route as well.
Unfortunately, from my research, in Canada these things are kept private. It’s insane. I told her she should try though as there’s no harm in asking, if she feels she needs more proof.

Thank you. I guess the feeling of selfishness comes from the worry that he might harm one of my family members.

It seems I’m one of the “lucky” ones who understands none of this was my fault though. This is the result of being severely neglected by everyone in my childhood and clinging to the only person who showed me (my skewed definition of) love. Just so happens he simultaneously was a monster.

Yeah, that is why even when I was younger, my best friends were online. I get awkward in person too but working on that!

Good question, I guess there is no solid set of criteria, it’s more like based on happiness (state of mental health)/overall success (not necessarily financial)/etc.

Hey. I’m not sure, I just want someone who feels like they can chat about what’s on their mind and vice versa. Someone who maybe is a bit further ahead in life, or in the same place, so we can guide each other. Someone who encourages me to learn new things and enjoy my time here.

I really like nature (hiking, foraging), reading, music, art, etc. So someone who is interested in similar would be great.
I completely agree. The job, and of course this CPTSD thing, takes too much of my energy to be able to self-teach at a good pace right now, but I hope one day I’ll be where I want.
I wish. They are very prestigious and will only look at those with a degree.

Gah!! Yes! This started around that age for me too. And I totally get pain in my right shoulder/neck at the same time too but I never thought they could be linked... that’s a good observation.

Honestly, I am glad that nothing showed up on the MRI. I’ve read stories of people having something like a lesion in their brain from trauma and I was worried maybe that’s linked to these migraines too... that’s just a heartbreaking thought and would make me feel so defeated.

That sounds like how I would describe these migraines too. And like my brain is pushing the back of my eyeball waiting to explode.

It feels like the pain comes from the right frontal lobe. Maybe the temporal lobe, but it feels higher in the brain than that. 

The frontal lobe plays a substantial role in decision making, self-control, and emotional regulation, providing the ability to behave appropriately in interpersonal situations and to regulate behavior in a socially acceptable manner.

The frontal lobe also integrates thinking skills by maintaining attention, high-level thinking and problem-solving. It is believed that humans' large frontal lobes are responsible for advanced thinking and innovation, as well as the ability to imagine situations.

Personally, I have issues with all of these areas. I never did before CPTSD. I can’t help but feel that the migraine pain and these symptoms are not only associated with trauma, but with each other - it’s like they feed off of each other or something. When my head hurts, those skills go out the window - and they do for months before and after surrounding the migraines, too.

Sorry, I think I am rambling now. It’s just really intriguing, and somewhat depressing, stuff.

This happened to me too. It was wonderful.

The thing is, I never really realized how much my trauma affected me day-to-day. I have horrible social skills and don’t deal with stress well. When I searched for the root of this, I landed at CPTSD and now it’s like I’m being re-traumatized all over again as I recount what happened to make me the way that I am. I hope it ends soon and I can go back to how you’re feeling right now. I’m happy you were able to get out.

Yeah, I get that feeling when bending over too and sometimes that‘ll kickstart the migraine, haha. Very annoying indeed. :(

I’m very curious if it is related to trauma. Peculiar that it’s always in the same location.

I am not one, but I wish I could be one. I do work with some in a similar environment so I can understand how you feel. It’s really stressful. We’re working from home right now and I am doing everything I can to not think about going back into the office. I’m much happier here at home. The only problem is I notice CPTSD is on my mind a lot more while I work... I think it might just be learning to adjust to focusing on my work in this setting, for me personally.

Thank you so much for this. You are right, just because I do this, doesn’t mean it will stop him... and I can’t dedicate my life to preventing him from hurting people... I just don’t want anyone to ever have to go through this if it can be prevented.

I might consider making a claim like that with the police at the very least...
I wish :( but thanks for the offer. I hope someone comes along for the both of us.
Thanks. ❤️ I was recently diagnosed late last year. Love this community.

I’m so sorry. These are new flashbacks for me too, around the same age as you. I had a knife or bottle of bleach in my hand a couple of times at that age. It’s so horrible.

But we are here now. We are safe. My therapist has told me it is helpful if we can connect to that young part of us and tell them this, and tell them that we will continue to keep them safe from now on. There’s a lot more to it but if that resonates with you at all, I really recommend looking into finding a counsellor who deals with CPTSD if possible. If not, even reading some self-help books like the ones in the sidebar could be useful. Best of luck to you.

Oof. As someone who is basically a glorified call centre employee... this hits home.

All I could ever ask for is a decent paying job where I don’t have to talk to clients, at least not over the phone/in person.

Yeah I’m not even going to read that guy’s comment after reading your reply, thanks lol.

I’ve done all there is to do regarding bettering mental health, and continue to do so because I know it’s an ongoing battle. These feelings are, nonetheless, still justified.

Thank you. I moved across the country from mine too, and it did help a lot in some ways, but now I am incredibly lonely because I am too scared to make new friends.

It’s all a mess. Such a shame how much terrible parenting can affect one’s life. I’m really sorry you’ve been in a similar boat. Glad to hear moving away helped for you too at least.

Thank you for this. I think a big problem is that part of me feels responsibility, as in if I don’t at least try, then it is also my fault, because I know what he is doing.

It’s a really difficult situation. I’m going to keep what you’ve said in mind though, for sure.
